text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Peter Hack, an executive of the Free Democrats (SZDSZ), said that unless a cleansing process starts among the Socialists and relations between the two governing parties are settled, it will be impossible to save the coalition. SZDSZ President Ivan Peto pressed for institutional guarantees that would, for example, rule out abuses in privatisation.
- The State Audit Office found several serious deficiencies in the part of the proposed 1997 central budget it was asked to evaluate. @

- Two individuals and three organisations received some of the HUF 804 million commission fee paid to lawyer Marta Tocsik for her role as mediator in municipal land deals between the State Privatisation and Holding Co. and local governments.
- Young Democrat President Viktor Orban told his party's national council Saturday that the Socialist Free-Democrat cabinet should be removed from power.
- Consumer prices grew by an average of 1.4 per cent in September, bringing the annual rate to 22.2 per cent, reports the Central Statistics Office. @
- A powerful grenade blew up in the hands of a Slovak national in Budapest's 10th district early Sunday, tearing the upper part of his body to pieces and killing him instantly.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- The Finance Ministry has submitted a proposal to the government to cut HUF 10 billion out of this year's central budget expenditure in order to keep the deficit below the 4 per cent of GDP figure stipulated by the IMF.
- Parliament is to sit for an extra day on Wednesday.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Representatives of the Agriculture and Finance Ministries agreed Friday on principles to be applied in distributing next year's agriculture subsidies.
- Hungarian iron and steel producers achieved a total net revenue of HUF 65.6 billion in the first half this year.
- A total of 25-30 percent of Hungary's GDP is produced by the black market, exports stated at a conference. (Sat.)
- AB Segerstrom and Svenson group, Scandinavia's largest manufacturer of metal components for electronic equipment, cars and household appliances, is planning to open a plant in Pecs.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Food production and trading companies exported a total of $1.61 billion in foodstuffs in the first eight months of the year, while a total of $594 million worth of food was imported.

- The German Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung and France's TF1 are expected to sign a contract within days on joint involvement in the privatisation of Hungarian Television Channel 2, Jozsef Pilissy, TF1 representative in Hungary, said in Cannes at the weekend.
NEPSZABADSAG

- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. expects three internationally known bidder to make an offer for 89 percent of the Magyar Hitel Bank by October 17, MHB managing director Zsigmond Jarai said. (Sat.)
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. still owns 560 companies, with total assets of over HUF 1,100 billion. (Sat.)
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
